reason: The keratinocyte layers and lipids look like the basis of the skin's water barrier, which addresses the chapter's opening goal.
expectation: I expect a layered skin surface that helps limit water loss.

alternatives.reason: Blood vessels and connective tissue also seem useful for living skin, but I want to start with the outer barrier.

effect: The epidermal barrier explains both water retention and how the surface is renewed. I now want to build the supporting skin tissue.
reaction: The connection between deeper cells and the shed surface is satisfying and clear.
reason: Connective tissue and blood vessels seem like a useful foundation for living skin.
expectation: I expect a vascular supporting layer beneath the epidermis.

alternatives.reason: The sweat gland also belongs in skin, but the supporting tissue seems more fundamental to build first.

effect: The connective tissue and vessels formed the supporting dermis I expected, so I can now join it to the epidermal barrier.
reaction: The result is straightforward, though it adds little explanation of the vessels' role.
reason: Joining the dermis and epidermis should build the main layers of skin.
expectation: I expect a layered skin structure with the barrier above the vascular dermis.

alternatives.reason: The sweat gland also needs assembly, but joining the skin layers seems like the next useful step.

effect: The layered skin has slots for a sweat outlet and sensory endings, and the result explains how its vessels support it. I can now add those structures.
reaction: The explanation makes the dermis feel more purposeful, though the picture description mentions the gland and nerves before they are fitted.
reason: Assembling the sweat gland and duct should prepare the sweat outlet for the skin.
expectation: I expect a connected sweat gland and duct that can be fitted into the layered skin.

alternatives.reason: The sensory endings can also be fitted now, but I want to assemble the gland first.

effect: The gland and duct are assembled, so I can fit the sweat outlet into the layered skin.
reaction: The result is straightforward and matches what I expected.
reason: Fitting the assembled gland should fill the sweat outlet slot.
expectation: I expect the gland to sit in the dermis with its duct opening at the skin surface.

alternatives.reason: The sensory endings also need fitting, but I want to finish placing the gland first.

effect: The sweat gland and duct are fitted, leaving the sensory endings to add.
reason: The sensory endings fill the remaining slot and support the goal of skin that can feel.
expectation: I expect layered skin with sensory endings and a sweat gland.

effect: The sensory endings are fitted, completing the listed skin structures and leaving the body ready to be covered.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should cover the body with the assembled skin.
expectation: I expect the body to gain living skin with a barrier, blood vessels, a sweat gland and sensory endings.

effect: The completed skin is connected to the body's vessels and nerves, completing the chapter goal.
reaction: The final connection is satisfying, though the result adds little explanation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the epidermal barrier was most worthwhile: it clearly connected water retention with renewal of the outer layer.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate fitting steps were predictable and added little explanation.

surprise.text: The layered-skin description mentioned the gland and nerves before I had fitted them, which made the assembly state confusing.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the parts had clear roles, although some fittings were routine.

continue.text: I would be somewhat interested in another chapter if it showed more relationships as clearly as the barrier and renewal explanation. The repeated fittings alone would not draw me onward.
